Container.Name: eugene-plexus
Container.Overview:
A self-hosted control plane for local LLM inference. It supervises engine processes it does not own, keeps a model library on your own disk as plainly-named files, holds per-model settings, and exposes one OpenAI-compatible endpoint that load-balances and fails over across local runtimes and cloud subscriptions — with real auth, so it works over a tailnet and not just localhost.
IT CAN RUN MODELS HERE, OR MANAGE THE MACHINES THAT DO. Point your tools at port 8080. As shipped it runs models on this server's CPU, which suits a small model. With an NVIDIA card shared through the Nvidia Driver plugin (the way Plex uses it), set NVIDIA GPU below and add --runtime=nvidia to Extra Parameters, and it fetches the llama.cpp build that fits the card. Other machines with GPUs run the installer and join port 8083.
PRE-RELEASE. The image is tagged `edge`, there is no released version, and the API may change. It is used daily by its author across two machines; it has not been used by anybody else.
FIRST START: open the WebUI and finish the wizard. It sets the passphrase that owns this install, so do it promptly — until then the first person to reach port 8079 can claim it.
MODELS: point the Models path at a share. The library in here uses it with no further setup, and your GPU machines mount that same share and the folder says where, once, under Library → Folders — so a model downloaded to this NAS is a model every node can serve.
RESTARTS: the trust root comes back sealed and routes nothing until somebody unlocks it, because a container has no OS keyring. Either unlock it on the Nodes page after each restart, or set up the passphrase file below once and stop thinking about it.

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: The web interface, and the browser's pass-through to every component. This is the port you open.

Config.Name: OpenAI-compatible endpoint
Config.Description: Point your tools and agent harnesses here. Speaks /v1/chat/completions and /v1/models, with tool calling and token streaming.

Config.Name: Control root
Config.Description: Where machines with GPUs enroll, and where a warm standby follows the log. If you change this, every node you have already enrolled is pointing at the old one — they record the address, not the name.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: THIS DIRECTORY IS THE INSTALL. It holds the identity and enrollment (agent.yaml, node.yaml), the trust root's replicated log, retained request metrics, and the logs. Keep it across updates and an update is an update; point at a fresh one and you have built a second install whose worker nodes are still enrolled to a root that no longer exists. Back it up. IT MUST BE OWNED BY 99:100 (nobody:users), which is what this container runs as: run `chown -R 99:100` on it before you start, and especially if it was created by an older container that ran as a different user.

Config.Name: Models
Config.Description: Where your model files live, or should land. Point this at a USER SHARE (the default is a share called models; make it under Shares if it does not exist) and the library in this container uses it with no further setup — the image tells it that /models is where the models are. Files already there are catalogued as they are: nothing is renamed, hashed or moved; delete Eugene Plexus and they are still where you put them. Downloads from Discover land here. THEN LET YOUR GPU MACHINES REACH THE SAME FILES: export that share (Shares → models → SMB Security Settings → Export: Yes, and a user who can read it, or NFS for Linux boxes), mount it on each GPU machine, and say where ONCE, on the folder — Library → Folders, the /models row: mounted on Windows nodes at \\TOWER\models (prefer the UNC path over a drive letter: the agent runs as a background task and a drive letter mapped in your desktop session may not exist there), mounted on Linux/macOS nodes at /mnt/models. Every node of that kind inherits it; a machine that mounts the share somewhere else gets one override under Library → that node → Folders, whose Browse lists that machine's own disk. Press Test to check it against the library's real files. Leave this path unset and the library reports /models missing, on purpose, rather than scanning an empty directory inside the container.

Config.Name: NVIDIA GPU (optional)
Config.Description: To run models on an NVIDIA card in this server: install the Nvidia Driver plugin (the one Plex uses), put the card's GPU UUID from that plugin's page here (or all for every card), and add --runtime=nvidia to Extra Parameters (Advanced View). Both, or neither: this alone does nothing, and --runtime=nvidia on a server without the plugin stops the container from starting. The container then fetches the llama.cpp build that fits the card, including older cards such as Pascal. Leave blank to run models on the CPU, or only on other machines.

Config.Name: Passphrase file (optional)
Config.Description: Set this AND the variable below to make restarts unattended. Put your passphrase in a file (use printf, not echo — one trailing newline is tolerated but nothing else is trimmed), chmod 400 it, and point this at it. Then set Security mode to 'Passphrase file auto-unlock' once in the web UI. Leave both blank and the trust root comes back sealed after every restart until you unlock it by hand. What it trades away: anyone who can read that file can unlock this install without knowing the passphrase.

Config.Name: Passphrase file path (optional)
Config.Description: The container-side path of the file above — /run/secrets/passphrase if you used the default. Set both or neither: set this alone and the root logs that the file is missing and stays sealed.

Config.Name: Model directory inside the container
Config.Description: Leave at /models. This is how the image tells the library which directory the Models path above is mounted at; change it ONLY if you changed the container-side path of Models, and to the same value. Several directories separate with a colon. It is a default, not a lock: whatever the library's Model directories are set to in the web UI wins, and clearing them returns to this.

Config.Name: Safe mode
Config.Description: Set to 1 to recover an install whose agent.yaml will not parse. The config endpoints stay reachable so the web UI can fix it. Leave at 0.
